bio.name: Faizan Alam
bio.intro: Mechatronics Engineering graduate with multidisciplinary expertise in robotics, AI, computer vision, embedded systems, and software engineering. Proven experience architecting and deploying intelligent robotic systems by integrating mechanical design, perception algorithms, control systems, and full-stack software into cohesive solutions. Skilled in ROS, Python, C++, TensorFlow, OpenCV, CAD, and system integration, with a strong foundation in autonomous robotics, machine learning, and hardware-software co-design. Dedicated to developing high-performance engineering solutions that bridge advanced research with practical deployment.

projects.title: Hand Gesture–Controlled Stewart Platform
projects.summary: 6-DOF Stewart platform with real-time hand gesture recognition at 98% accuracy.
projects.challenge:
Develop a low-cost six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) motion control system for a Stewart platform using natural hand gestures, while maintaining a total project budget of under CAD $1,000. The system must accurately recognize complex hand gestures without relying on commercial motion-capture hardware. These gestures must be translated into smooth and precise control of all six degrees of freedom. 

Surge, sway, heave, roll, pitch, and yaw, in real time. Also there is the challenge of maintaining platform stability, minimizing latency, and ensuring accurate motion despite the complexity of coordinating six actuators simultaneously.
projects.approach:
Developed a real-time hand gesture recognition system in Python using MediaPipe, mapping six distinct gestures to the Stewart platform's six degrees of freedom (surge, sway, heave, roll, pitch, and yaw) with low-latency control.

Designed, programmed, and iteratively optimized a servo-driven 6-DOF Stewart platform using Arduino, improving motion accuracy, stability, and responsiveness through multiple hardware and software iterations.

Engineered and modelled some of the structural components and custom mounting hardware in Onshape, producing a cost-effective mechanical design suitable for fabrication and assembly.
projects.outcome:
98% gesture recognition accuracy across 6 DOF with all 6 actuators. 

Delivered within 50% of the total budget, including replacement purchases. 

Garnered multiple praises, including from the 100+ participants who operated the final prototype at the Capstone exhibition.

projects.title: Mobile Robotics — ROS / LiDAR
projects.summary: ROS-based TurtleBot for autonomous navigation, object detection, and LiDAR path planning.
projects.challenge: Develop an autonomous mobile robot platform using ROS on Linux, integrating navigation, colour recognition, and object detection capabilities. Implement robotic perception and control systems to enable the robot to interpret its environment, identify objects, and navigate autonomously through complex scenarios.
projects.approach: Co-developed a **ROS-based TurtleBot** system integrating path planning, trajectory tracking, colour recognition, and object detection. Programmed and tested autonomous navigation algorithms while separately developing **LiDAR-based navigation simulations** for a skid-steer vehicle to evaluate motion planning and obstacle avoidance.
projects.outcome: Successfully completed all milestone demonstrations within 3 minutes, showcasing efficient system integration and reliable autonomous performance. Achieved a ranking within the top 10% of the class through strong technical execution, problem-solving, and project implementation.

projects.title: PEIE STEM Camp Portal
projects.summary: Full-stack camp management portal with key-gated sections for eah class and Google Sheets attendance that auto checks in students after they are signed in..
projects.challenge: Faced challenges delivering lessons due to limited access to presentation materials, as slides could not be displayed on a shared screen and presentation files were unavailable on student devices. Adapted lesson delivery strategies to ensure students could still access the required information and remain engaged throughout the sessions.
projects.approach: Developed a fully static, serverless web application utilizing the **GitHub Contents API** for data storage and management. Implemented secure student and administrator portals with key-based access control, along with an automated attendance tracking system integrated with **Google Sheets, Google Forms, and Google Apps Script** to streamline data collection and management.
projects.outcome: Delivered a user-friendly web application that centralized camp operations by streamlining attendance tracking, lesson material access, and administrative workflows within a single, integrated platform.

projects.title: Work Flow Assist PWA
projects.summary: Personal productivity PWA with priority engine, task estimator, and daily planner.
projects.challenge: Developed a fully client-side productivity tool capable of operating offline while maintaining persistent data storage without requiring backend infrastructure. Designed an efficient local data management system to ensure reliable access, seamless user experience, and data retention across sessions.
projects.approach: Developed a **Progressive Web App (PWA)** featuring an Eisenhower Matrix-based priority engine, a guided task estimation system, and a Daily Assistant planner with **Focus** and **Spread** modes. Implemented **localStorage-based persistence** to enable offline functionality, reliable data retention, and a seamless user experience without backend dependencies.
projects.outcome: Delivered a fully functional **offline-capable Progressive Web App (PWA)** designed for personal productivity and task management. The application was deployed for daily use, demonstrating reliable performance, persistent data storage, and practical usability in real-world scenarios.

projects.title: FRC Mentor
projects.summary: Mentored student led teams to develop robots that were able to intake, transfer and shoot game pieces, both autonomously and driver controlled. Also assisted in the presentation preperation for Judging in order to present the student's brilliance and exceptional work.
projects.challenge:
The 2026 FRC challenge required teams to design and build a robot capable of navigating past a field barricade, collecting game pieces from the playing field, and accurately scoring them into designated hoppers. 

The robot needed to be versatile, durable, and capable of withstanding defensive contact during matches. Additionally, teams were required to develop an autonomous system that allowed the robot to operate independently during the first 30 seconds of the 2.5-minute match.
projects.approach: Focused on applying the Engineering Design Process to teach students the importance of developing strong initial concepts and design strategies. Students progressed from designing and planning their solutions to building prototypes, testing their designs, and analyzing performance. Through multiple rounds of iteration and refinement, teams improved their prototypes until achieving their final competition-ready designs.
projects.outcome: Teams successfully qualified for the Provincial Championship, earned multiple awards, and achieved recognition among the top 100 teams in Canada. Their accomplishments reflected the effectiveness of the design process, iterative development, and technical skills developed throughout the season.
